claims.text: Increasing substrate temperature during deposition refines the grain structure of non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films.
Increasing substrate temperature enhances local chemical short-range order in non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films.
Refined grains and enhanced chemical short-range order spatially distribute nucleation sites for the magnetostructural transition.
Spatially distributed transition events broaden the magnetostructural transition.
Spatially distributed transition events reduce magnetocaloric hysteresis under low-applied-field cooling cycles.
The proposed microstructural changes largely preserve the overall magnetocaloric entropy change.
Lower-substrate-temperature, as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films have an ordered single-phase hexagonal structure.
The lower-substrate-temperature films exhibit a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
The lower-substrate-temperature films exhibit high hysteresis.
A controlled post-deposition anneal is equivalent to increasing substrate temperature during deposition for inducing the proposed mediator.
Thin-film geometry ensures rapid heat exchange.
Higher substrate temperature increases atomic mobility during deposition.
Increased atomic mobility produces a more refined microstructure and improved chemical ordering.
Elevated-substrate-temperature films will have a broader magnetostructural transition than the baseline films.
Elevated-substrate-temperature films will have significantly lower hysteresis width than the baseline films.
Elevated-substrate-temperature films will retain a high, although possibly slightly reduced, magnetocaloric entropy change.
Composition changes or use of arc-melted and melt-spun forms may produce responses different from those predicted for the films.
The quantitative entropy-change and hysteresis responses depend on deposition or annealing conditions and film thickness.
